title: people-ops-hiring-onboarding-performance-and-manager-guide-2026-v80
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary
This document describes Redwood Inference's end-to-end people operations practices for hiring, employee onboarding, the performance and feedback cycle, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers.

Scope
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors with >6 month engagements, and managers involved in hiring or reviews.
- Does not replace role-specific interview rubrics (see related pages).

Purpose
- Provide a consistent, equitable hiring experience that prioritizes candidate experience and quality-of-hire.
- Ensure new hires reach productivity quickly with measurable onboarding milestones.
- Create a continuous feedback culture backed by an annual performance cycle and calibration.

Ownership
- People Ops: process owner, training, offer templates, L&D coordination.
- Hiring manager: role definition, interview loop, final hiring decision responsibilities.
- Recruiting: candidate sourcing, scheduling, offer administration.

Part 1 - Hiring process (high level)
1) Requisition and role definition
   - Manager opens a hiring requisition in Workday with a clear role summary, success metrics (3 measurable goals for first 6 months), required vs. preferred skills, and compensation band request.
   - People Ops reviews and approves requisition within 3 business days.

2) Sourcing and screening
   - Recruiting owns job posting, initial outreach, and résumé prescreen.
   - Prescreen call (20-30 min) uses standardized prescreen checklist: eligibility, compensation expectations, right-to-work, core experience, and interest. Notes must be recorded in Greenhouse.

3) Interview loop and scorecard
   - Standard loop for IC engineering roles: Hiring manager screen, technical take-home (optional), live technical interview(s), system design (senior+), collaboration/culture interview, hiring manager wrap-up.
   - Each interview uses the role-specific scorecard. Required fields on the scorecard: competency ratings (1-5), strengths, risks/concerns, and hire/no-hire recommendation.
   - Interviewers should commit to hiring decisions within 48 hours of the final interview.

4) Decision & calibration
   - Hiring manager synthesizes scorecards and consults Recruiting and People Ops for compensation/leveling guidance.
   - For hires above L5 or >$250k total comp, obtain final approval from People Ops Director and Finance.

5) Offer process
   - Recruiting drafts offer using the approved template and includes: base, equity (if eligible), sign-on, target start date, manager onboarding plan, and relocation stipend (if applicable).
   - Offer expiration: standard 7 calendar days unless manager requests extension.

6) Onboarding initiation
   - Once offer accepted, Recruiting triggers the New Hire intake form and notifies People Ops and IT.

Interview best practices and anti-bias guidance
- Ask behaviorally anchored questions tied to the scorecard.
- Avoid illegal or off-limits questions (family plans, health, age).
- Use structured evaluation and avoid comparing to a single prior candidate.
- DEI note: ensure diverse candidate slates for senior roles where feasible.

Part 2 - New hire onboarding (30-60-90 framework and checklists)
Intro: Onboarding is a shared responsibility: People Ops owns the program, Hiring Manager owns role ramp and first 90 days, IT and Buddy own tools access and cultural orientation.

Pre-day 0 (People Ops & Recruiting)
- Complete background check and I-9/eligibility.
- Send welcome packet: offer letter, benefits overview, first-week agenda, team org chart, and hardware checklist.
- Create accounts: SSO, email, Slack, productivity tools, HRIS record.

Day 1 checklist (Hiring Manager)
- Team welcome and intro meeting (30-45 min).
- Equipment check and workspace orientation.
- HR benefits orientation (People Ops).
- First-day 90-day objectives reviewed (manager).
- Assign buddy and schedule 1:1 cadence (weekly for first 8 weeks).

Week 1 objectives
- Complete security and compliance training.
- Read: product overview, architecture primer, and team OKRs.
- Deliverable: walk through the codebase or product flow; run a local dev environment smoke test.

30-day checklist
- Goals: complete onboarding learning path, deliver a small ownership task, present a short demo to the team.
- Manager: 30-day feedback conversation; update success metrics if needed.

60-day checklist
- Goals: take on a customer-facing or cross-functional task, pair-program or lead a small project.
- Manager: document progress and ramp adjustments in Lattice (or HRIS).

90-day checklist and formal check-in
- Formal 90-day review with manager and People Ops: confirm expected level, finalize long-term goals, and decide on ongoing development plan.
- Outcome: transition plan for full team ownership and promotion pathway if applicable.

Buddy program and mentorship
- Every new hire is assigned a buddy from the hiring team for 90 days. Buddies are not the manager and are expected to: answer day-to-day questions, schedule coffee chats, and provide context on team norms.

Remote hire specifics
- Include virtual onboarding checklist, timezone-aware meeting scheduling, and shipping hardware before start date.
- Manager must explicitly schedule one overlap week of real-time overlap for first two weeks when hiring across >6 hour timezone differences.

Part 3 - Performance and feedback cycle
Overview
- Redwood runs a continuous feedback culture with a formal annual performance cycle: goal-setting (Q1 kickoff or hire start), mid-year check-in, end-of-year review, and calibration.

Quarterly/annual goals (OKRs)
- Individual contributor goals should align to team OKRs and include 3 measurable goals (owner, metric, target).

Performance timeline (calendar example)
- Jan 15-Feb 15: Annual goal setting and manager/employee agreement.
- Jun 1-Jun 15: Mid-year check-in and development update.
- Nov 1-Nov 30: End-of-year self-review submission.
- Dec 10-Dec 31: Manager reviews and calibration meetings.

Continuous feedback expectations
- Managers should provide timely feedback (informal) every 2-3 weeks and document major feedback in the HRIS within 7 days.
- Employees are encouraged to request feedback and submit upward feedback during 1:1s.

Formal evaluations and rating scale
- Ratings use a 5-point scale: 1 (does not meet) - 3 (meets expectations) - 5 (consistently exceeds expectations).
- Managers must provide written justification and examples for ratings of 1 or 5.

Calibration and fairness
- Calibration panels include cross-functional managers and People Ops to ensure leveling consistency and pay equity.
- For population >100 employees, People Ops runs an audit report on rating distribution and pay impact before final approvals.

Promotion and leveling
- Promotion criteria require demonstrated impact, scope growth, and manager + peer endorsements.
- For every promotion, update the role profile, compensation adjustments, and career ladder documentation.

Performance improvement and exits
- Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) process: manager discusses concerns, documents expectations and timeline (normally 60-90 days), People Ops advises on steps, and HR monitors progress.
- Offboarding: include knowledge transfer checklist and access deprovisioning runbook (see eng-infra runbooks).

Part 4 - Manager guide (practical checklist)
Hiring
- Build a clear success profile with measurable 6-month goals before opening req.
- In interviews: ask for examples, probe for impact, and use the scorecard.

First 30/60/90
- Set clear priorities for weeks 1, 4, 8 and review weekly.
- Hold weekly 1:1s (first 8 weeks), then move to biweekly if appropriate.

Feedback and development
- Give balanced feedback: one positive, one area for improvement.
- Use Lattice (or HRIS) for documentation of coaching conversations.
- Create a development plan with two growth goals and quarterly milestones.

Recognition and retention
- Nominate high-impact contributors for peer recognition and the quarterly rewards program.
- Flag retention risks: extended time-to-productivity, engagement drops, compensation market drift.

Escalation and support
- For interpersonal conflicts, contact People Ops within 3 business days.
- For suspected misconduct, follow the incident-reporting policy and escalate to Security & Legal.

Part 5 - Policies and mandatory trainings
- Probationary period: 90 days for new hires. Manager completes a probation checklist at day 60 and day 90.
- Time-off & remote work: follow companywide PTO policy (see related pages).
- Mandatory trainings: Security Awareness, Data Handling, and Privacy & Compliance completed within first 14 days.

Documentation and templates (what to use and where)
- Job requisition template (Workday).
- Interview scorecard (Greenhouse).
- Offer letter & compensation templates (People Ops Drive).
- 30/60/90 checklist and manager onboarding templates (People Ops wiki).

Measuring success (KPIs)
- Time-to-fill (target: median 45 days for IC roles).
- Hiring manager satisfaction (post-hire survey target >4.0/5).
- New hire time-to-productivity (target: 90% of new hires reach expected 6-month goals by month 6).
- Offer acceptance rate (target >70%).

Training and enablement for interviewers and managers
- Quarterly interviewer calibration training run by People Ops.
- New manager onboarding: 2-week program with HR, Finance, and Security touchpoints.

Appendix A - Common templates and sample phrasing
- Offer acceptance email subject: "Welcome to Redwood - Offer Details for [Candidate Name]"
- 30-day feedback script: "You've done a great job on X; I'd like to see you take more ownership of Y by the next 30 days. Here's a specific action: [specific action]"

Appendix B - Frequently asked questions
Q: How do I request an exception to hiring freeze?
A: Submit a business case to People Ops and Finance; expect a 5 business day review.

Q: Who approves equity increases?
A: People Ops in consultation with Finance and the hiring manager; final approval threshold >$100k equity value per annum.
